content: An infobox on Wikipedia is a structured table designed to present summary information in a consistent format across articles that share a common subject. A taxobox, which is a specific type of infobox, is used to summarize information about an organism or a group of organisms, and the infobox concept is a generalization of this. If you are creating an infobox for a new project, it is important to first propose it on the Wikipedia:List of infoboxes/Proposed sub-page. Once the infobox has been implemented, it should be moved to the appropriate sub-page of the main list. When selecting colors for your infobox, avoid using colors that are already in use. You should document your chosen color on the list to inform others that it has been taken. You may opt to use a single color for all tables within a project or implement a color-coding system. For instance, the organism taxobox employs different colors to represent each biological kingdom. For further guidance on color selection, refer to the article on web colors. An infobox may or may not utilize the template software feature. Infobox templates serve as an alternative to static infoboxes and allow for a standardized appearance across related subject items with minimal coding required within individual articles. For more details, refer to Wikipedia:Infobox templates. If your infobox is aligned to the right side of the page, it is advisable to limit its width to no more than one-third of the available page width. The basic template for creating an infobox can be found at Template:Infobox. This template includes optional parameters and can be compared to the use of conditional statements, as described in Wikipedia:Qif conditionals. For a specific example of a taxobox, refer to the instructions provided at Wikipedia:WikiProject Tree of Life/taxobox usage.
